question: Given real-config smoke evidence that a simple read approves but a representative code-audit task times out during planning/search, which new bounded TUI slice is locally justified?

confirmed_facts.fact: The real user config can initialize the provider and two MCP servers; a single read-only README task approved in two steps, while a read-only TUI audit timed out after planning/search at 30 seconds without a run manifest.
NotebookLM proposes semantic hanging indent, physical block closures, and lifecycle-anchor navigation as hypotheses for the repeated-search audit pain.
Current code already has semantic rails, bounded cell-width wrapping, block focus navigation, and lifecycle/activity history surfaces.
confirmed_facts.evidence: CodeGraph exploration of render_live_line, reasoning_commit_lines, LiveTranscript::move_semantic_focus, and input routing

contradictions: NotebookLM's physical-closure proposal is not a reproduced layout defect; current static reasoning already emits a closing rail and the live renderer tracks block ends.
NotebookLM's Alt+Up/Alt+Down lifecycle navigation conflicts with existing tool-focus routing; Alt+Left/Alt+Right already moves semantic focus in the held live inspector.
The hanging-indent proposal identifies a plausible alignment preference, but no current ConPTY or deterministic regression proves that it causes the reported stall or audit failure.

unverified_hypotheses.hypothesis: Static reasoning continuation rows should hang under the first body column instead of only preserving the two-cell rail.
support: reasoning_commit_lines places metadata on the first row only
against: existing rail and narrow reflow tests pass
unverified_hypotheses.experiment: Add a deterministic cell-position regression for multiline reasoning at 18/32/40/80 columns before changing projection.

candidates.core: semantic hanging indent for multiline reasoning
constraints: reuse current semantic rails and cell-width wrapper
risks: narrow widths may lose body text
anchor may be truncated from bounded live history

local_adjudication.reason: Potentially useful presentation refinement, but current rail/word-boundary behavior is already covered and no concrete failure was observed.
Existing lifecycle rails and block-end handling cover the proposed boundary; extra rows risk viewport jumps.
Proposed Alt+Up/Down keys conflict with tool focus; existing Alt+Left/Alt+Right semantic focus already provides bounded block navigation.

implementation.core: Keep the deterministic loop-counter HUD as the current completed usability slice; do not implement a new NLM candidate without a local visual regression.
constraints: preserve execution semantics and current key routing
do not add hidden-reasoning heuristics, new renderer, sidebar, or virtualizer
retain native scrollback, bounded histories, ANSI16, CJK cell-width behavior, and ConPTY coverage
validation: retain smoke evidence as diagnostic only
run a focused hanging-indent regression before any future implementation
require workspace tests, clippy, build, and ConPTY for a future visual change

recommendation: Do not force any of the three NLM hypotheses into code this round; the local evidence supports the already-implemented deterministic counters, while the remaining candidates need reproduction.

next_step.value: If continuing, measure multiline reasoning body-column alignment at narrow widths; otherwise archive this adjudication and reconcile the completed Note.

stop_conditions: Do not interpret counters as hidden reasoning or add new stop rules.
Do not add physical closures or lifecycle key bindings without a reproducible local defect.
Do not claim the real-config audit completed; it timed out before manifest creation.
